name: The Human Review Rule
title: The Human Review Rule
answer: The Human Review Rule holds that AI may inform a decision about a child or an employee, but a named person must make the final call. The district writes down which decisions always require human review, adopts that list at the board level, and audits each year to confirm the rule is followed. It matters because a rule on paper can fade once AI tools produce daily scores and flags that people start treating as decisions.

crumbs.name: Privacy, Safety, and the Human Review Rule

sections.body: The Human Review Rule turns a broad principle into district policy: AI can supply information, but a named person remains the decision maker. The district identifies the decisions that must always pass through a person, and the list should cover grades, special education decisions, discipline, placement, teacher evaluation, threat assessment, and hiring. The board adopts the list, and the district checks each year that the rule is actually being followed. The problem it solves is drift, where constant AI scores and flags quietly become the decision itself. Writing the list down and reviewing it annually keeps human judgment from eroding in daily practice.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, the rule works by having the person record their own judgment before looking at the AI's suggestion. The text does not give grade band examples, but the decisions named span classrooms and district offices, from grades and discipline to placement, teacher evaluation, threat assessment, and hiring. The review process has four steps, shown in Figure 3.5, which turn the principle into a routine. Each year a small team pulls a sample of decisions and checks whether a person actually reviewed each one. That annual audit is what keeps the rule alive rather than letting it fade.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels this idea with evidence from a set of experiments. In those experiments, people asked to correct a machine's decision often went along with bad decisions, while people who decided first and then saw the machine's view corrected mistakes (Krugel et al., 2023). The lesson the text draws for schools is to have the person record their own judgment before looking at the AI's suggestion. Figure 3.5 turns that lesson into four steps. The annual audit is presented as the practice that keeps the rule from fading, not as a separate research finding.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits and risks are set out plainly: a rule on paper can still fade in practice. Once a tool produces scores and flags every day, it becomes easy to treat them as decisions, which is the central danger the rule guards against. The decisions that stay with a person are the ones on the district list, including grades, special education decisions, discipline, placement, teacher evaluation, threat assessment, and hiring. The annual audit, in which a small team samples decisions and checks whether a person actually reviewed each one, is the safeguard that keeps the rule alive. Nothing here is legal advice; it describes practice.
